In the caves beneath the Tree of Life, everything lies still. Nothing will see or hear that which occurs.

Some Flora at ground level feel vibrations pushing through the Earth. They rush down to the caves, where they find something new.

Above Anar and Rana's reflecting pools are perfectly shaped disks of metal, bonded somehow to the walls of the cavern. The disks reflect just like the pools do, so anything between them is repeated a thousand times in a thousand mirrors.

The Flora gaze in awe at this creation, and wonder which god is responsible. They receive no response, until a particularly curious individual sticks its head out, and gazes into its own eyes. Immediately, it finds itself someplace else.

Everything that every was, everything that ever will be, everything that could have been, everything that is.

It all lies before it, spread out in a colossal web, of webs, and every time the Flora believes it has seen the whole thing it discovers that but a single strand lies within its gaze. It spins around and around, futilely trying to behold the majesty of existence. Then it realizes that something else is there. A being of the same nature as the web, one of which every attempt to perceive in full fails, one which can *understand* this web. It speaks, with a thousand voices.

*Greetings, young Flora, do you seek enlightenment?*

The Flora shrieks and flees, finding itself falling into the reflecting pool and disturbing its waters. The other Flora pull it out, asking what it saw. It does not respond. It cannot respond. It never speaks again.

Within the mirrors, in the Realm of Everything, the being is disappointed. It knows that there are [geniuses](https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/751115/3683658) among the Flora, but clearly this was not one of them. A piece of its awareness, which is all of its awareness, will remain here, waiting for one worthy to gaze upon it. The rest moves elsewhere, to other tasks.

The world will learn to see itself, one way or the other.
